subject: indian-polity
summary: The Constituent Assembly framed the Constitution between December 1946 and November 1949.

bodyBlocks.text: Making of the Constitution
The Constituent Assembly framed the Constitution between December 1946 and November 1949.
Dr B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee, which reviewed and refined drafts prepared on the basis of the Objectives Resolution.
The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.

bodyBlocks.title: Key points
items: Constituent Assembly first met on 9 December 1946
Drafting Committee chaired by Dr B. R. Ambedkar

subject: indian-polity
summary: The Preamble states the ideals of the Constitution: justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.

bodyBlocks.text: Preamble and basic structure
The Preamble states the ideals of the Constitution: justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.
In Kesavananda Bharati (1973) the Supreme Court held that Parliament cannot alter the basic structure of the Constitution.
Federalism, secularism, judicial review and the rule of law have all been treated as part of the basic structure.

bodyBlocks.title: Key points
items: Preamble declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic
Basic structure doctrine limits the amending power

subject: indian-polity
summary: Part III of the Constitution guarantees Fundamental Rights, enforceable against the State.

bodyBlocks.text: Nature of rights
Part III of the Constitution guarantees Fundamental Rights, enforceable against the State.
They are not absolute; the State may impose reasonable restrictions in the public interest.
Rights are grouped as equality, freedom, against exploitation, religion, cultural and educational rights, and constitutional remedies.

subject: indian-polity
summary: Article 19(1) guarantees six freedoms to citizens, including speech and expression, assembly and movement.

bodyBlocks.text: Article 19 restrictions
Article 19(1) guarantees six freedoms to citizens, including speech and expression, assembly and movement.
Clauses 19(2) to 19(6) allow reasonable restrictions on grounds such as sovereignty, public order, decency and morality.
Courts test whether a restriction is reasonable, proportionate and not arbitrary.

bodyBlocks.title: Key points
items: Article 19 is available to citizens only
Eight grounds for restricting speech under 19(2)
Reasonableness is subject to judicial review

subject: indian-polity
summary: The President is the constitutional head of the Union executive, acting on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.

bodyBlocks.text: President and Council of Ministers
The President is the constitutional head of the Union executive, acting on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.
The Prime Minister heads the Council of Ministers, which is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
The President has limited discretion, for example when no party commands a majority.

bodyBlocks.title: Key points
items: Article 74 provides for aid and advice

subject: indian-polity
summary: The Supreme Court is the apex court with original, appellate and advisory jurisdiction.

bodyBlocks.text: Supreme Court and judicial review
The Supreme Court is the apex court with original, appellate and advisory jurisdiction.
Judicial review lets courts invalidate laws and executive actions that violate the Constitution.
Public interest litigation has widened access to justice.

bodyBlocks.title: Key points
items: Article 137 allows review of its own judgments
Judicial review is part of the basic structure

subject: history
summary: The Indus Valley Civilisation flourished from about 2600 to 1900 BCE across the north-western subcontinent.

bodyBlocks.text: Indus Valley Civilisation
The Indus Valley Civilisation flourished from about 2600 to 1900 BCE across the north-western subcontinent.
Cities such as Harappa and Mohenjo-daro show planned grids, drainage and standardised weights.
The script remains undeciphered, so much of our understanding rests on archaeology.

bodyBlocks.title: Key points
items: Major sites: Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Dholavira, Lothal

subject: history
summary: The Mauryan empire under Chandragupta and Ashoka was the first large pan-Indian state.

bodyBlocks.text: Mauryan administration
The Mauryan empire under Chandragupta and Ashoka was the first large pan-Indian state.
The Arthashastra describes a centralised bureaucracy, espionage and revenue administration.
Ashoka's dhamma emphasised tolerance and welfare after the Kalinga war.

subject: history
summary: The Revolt of 1857 began at Meerut in May 1857 and spread across northern and central India.

bodyBlocks.text: Revolt of 1857
The Revolt of 1857 began at Meerut in May 1857 and spread across northern and central India.
Causes included political annexation, economic exploitation, and the greased cartridge grievance among sepoys.
After the revolt the Government of India Act 1858 transferred control from the Company to the Crown.

bodyBlocks.title: Key points
items: Doctrine of Lapse as a political cause

subject: geography
summary: The Indian monsoon is a seasonal reversal of winds driven by differential heating of land and sea.

bodyBlocks.text: Indian monsoon mechanism
The Indian monsoon is a seasonal reversal of winds driven by differential heating of land and sea.
The shift of the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone and the Tibetan plateau heating influence its onset.
El Nino years are often associated with weaker monsoon rainfall.

bodyBlocks.title: Key points
items: Southwest monsoon arrives in Kerala around 1 June
ITCZ shift draws moist winds inland

subject: economy
summary: Inflation is a sustained rise in the general price level, tracked in India through the Consumer Price Index.

bodyBlocks.text: Inflation and monetary policy
Inflation is a sustained rise in the general price level, tracked in India through the Consumer Price Index.
The Reserve Bank of India uses the repo rate and other tools to keep inflation near its target.
The Monetary Policy Committee sets the policy rate with a mandate of 4 percent inflation, within a band of 2 to 6 percent.

bodyBlocks.title: Key points
items: CPI is the anchor for inflation targeting
Repo rate is the key policy tool

subject: environment
summary: A biodiversity hotspot has high species endemism and has lost a large share of its original habitat.

bodyBlocks.text: Biodiversity hotspots
A biodiversity hotspot has high species endemism and has lost a large share of its original habitat.
India includes parts of four hotspots: the Himalaya, Indo-Burma, the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, and Sundaland.
Protected areas, community reserves and the Biological Diversity Act 2002 support conservation.

bodyBlocks.title: Key points
items: Western Ghats is a global hotspot
Protected areas include national parks and sanctuaries

subject: science-technology
summary: ISRO develops launch vehicles and satellites for communication, earth observation and navigation.

bodyBlocks.text: India's space programme
ISRO develops launch vehicles and satellites for communication, earth observation and navigation.
Chandrayaan and Mangalyaan demonstrated cost-effective interplanetary missions.
Recent reforms opened parts of the space sector to private participation through IN-SPACe.

bodyBlocks.title: Key points
items: PSLV and GSLV are workhorse launch vehicles

subject: ethics
summary: Ethics in administration concerns integrity, impartiality, objectivity and accountability.

bodyBlocks.text: Ethics in public administration
Ethics in administration concerns integrity, impartiality, objectivity and accountability.
Civil servants face dilemmas where law, personal values and public interest may pull in different directions.
Codes of conduct and the Seven Principles of Public Life provide guidance.

bodyBlocks.title: Key points
items: Integrity and impartiality are core values
Conflict of interest must be disclosed
Accountability to citizens and the law
